generationChain.prompt: Create one finished replacement cover illustration for an early-childhood ESL nonfiction reader titled How a Flowering Plant Grows. This is a picture-only cover, 16:9 landscape, no text, no numbers, no symbols or labels. Use bold clean clear 2D cartoon art across the entire image: crisp continuous black outlines, flat clean natural colors, very restrained cel shading, white/pale-sky background with a simple garden soil cross section. Show one coherent four-stage growth comparison from left to right: a large pale garden pea seed just starting a small downward root in soil; a small rooted sprout above soil with first leaves; a healthy pea vine with paired oval leaflets, curling tendrils and a few natural white pea flowers; then a mature pea vine with attached green pea pods, one naturally opened pod showing several round peas. Keep the plants recognisably the same kind, botanically plausible, progressively taller left to right, grounded in soil with roots below and green shoots above. A simple plain yellow Sun disk high in the sky may provide light but has NO face. Plants, flowers, seeds, Sun, clouds and scenery have NO faces, eyes, mouths or anthropomorphic features. No children or characters are needed. Clear large silhouettes, generous uncluttered framing, no arrows, decorative badges, lettering, logos, religion or political or identity emblems. Do not imitate a photograph or painterly texture. The nonfiction inquiry is seed, root, shoot, leaves, flowers, pods and new seeds; show growth and the completed seed cycle clearly.

candidateReview.verdict: selected candidate for independent parent adjudication
candidateReview.observations: Four clear plant stages, connected roots/stems, natural leaf/flower/pod features, faceless Sun, no embedded numbers/labels/faces. General flowering legume/pea example suitable for generic inquiry; source p6 has bean-like red flowers while p7 has pea-like pods, so no exact whole-book cultivar claim is made. Illustrative stages are not asserted to be same-time physical plant.
